title: System Calls and Data Directives in MIPS
description: Use .data and .asciiz to store a string in memory, then invoke syscall 4 and syscall 10 from main.

steps.description: In `main`, `li $v0, 4` loads `4` into `$v0`, `la $a0, msg` loads the memory address of label `msg` into `$a0`, and `syscall` runs on line 9.
Lines 12-13 load `10` into `$v0` and invoke `syscall` again, while `.data` at lines 15-16 defines `msg` as a null-terminated `.asciiz` string `"Hello, world!"`.
Notice how `la $a0, msg` passes the address of `msg` in the `.data` segment via `$a0`, while `$v0` selects which `syscall` operation to perform.

steps.question: What does `la $a0, msg` on line 8 place into register `$a0`?
steps.answer: The memory address where the string `"Hello, world!"` starts in the `.data` section.

steps.description: With `$v0 = 4` and `$a0` holding the address of `msg`, `syscall` prints `Hello, world!`.
With `$v0 = 10`, the second `syscall` terminates the program.
